title: FlowGenesis: Representation-Driven Self-Organization of Neural Architectures
abstract: arXiv:2610.35108v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deep neural networks typically rely on architectures specified before training, despite the continuous evolution of their internal representations. We introduce FlowGenesis, a framework in which neural architectures adapt through neuron birth and pruning guided by Representation Flux, a local statistic capturing changes in minibatch mean activations. Neurons exhibiting persistently high Flux undergo splitting designed to approximately preserve the network function, while neurons with low Flux and low activity are pruned. This mechanism allows network capacity to evolve without prescribing a target architecture or performing a separate architecture search. Experiments on image and text classi- fication show that networks initialized with different sizes approach similar final neuron-count ranges within each dataset while maintaining comparable predictive performance. translated_title: FlowGenesis：基于表征驱动的神经架构自组织
translated_abstract: 深度神经网络通常依赖于在训练开始前就已确定的架构，尽管其内部表征在持续演化。我们提出了FlowGenesis，这是一个神经架构通过神经元的诞生与剪枝进行自适应调整的框架，其引导依据是“表征通量”——一种捕捉小批量平均激活值变化的局部统计量。具有持续高通量的神经元会经历旨在近似保持网络功能的分裂，而通量低且活跃度低的神经元则被剪枝。这一机制使网络容量能够自主演化，无需预先指定目标架构，也无需进行单独的架构搜索。在图像和文本分类任务上的实验表明，以不同规模初始化的网络在每个数据集上都会趋近于相似的最终神经元数量范围，同时保持相当的预测性能。我们进一步将FlowGenesis扩展到持续学习领域，其中表征……
tldr: FlowGenesis框架通过基于表征通量的神经元分裂与剪枝机制，使神经网络架构在训练中自适应演化，无需预设目标架构或额外架构搜索。
en_tdlr: FlowGenesis is a framework that enables neural architectures to self-organize during training through representation-flux-guided neuron splitting and pruning, eliminating the need for predefined target architectures or separate architecture searches.
